questions.question:
After interchanging the given two signs what will be the values of equation (I) and (II) respectively?

× and ÷

I. 16 ÷ 4 - 8 × 2 + 7

II. 8 ÷ 4 - 9 × 3 + 8
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9f1f11fbb4e091305a6b414e74c3aec25b8d519670a1f3bd65f5bd4eb1bdcd68.png] 

Given: × and ÷

I. 16 ÷ 4 - 8 × 2 + 7

After interchanging the given two signs we get:

⇒ 16 × 4 - __**8 ÷ 2**__ + 7

⇒ __**16 × 4**__ - 4 + 7

⇒ __64__ - 4 __**+ 7**__

⇒ __**71 - 4**__ = **67**

II. 8 ÷ 4 - 9 × 3 + 8 

After interchanging the given two signs we get:

⇒ 8 × 4 - __**9 ÷ 3**__ + 8

⇒ __**8 × 4**__ - 3 + 8

⇒ __32__ - 3 __**+ 8**__

⇒ __**40 - 3**__ = 37

Hence, the correct answer is "**67 and 37**".

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct is regarding measures of money supply?

I. M1 and M2 are known as narrow money.

II. M3 and M4 are known as broad money.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct statements regarding measures of money supply are that M1 and M2 are known as narrow money, and M3 and M4 are known as broad money: 
 
• **M1**
 
 
• Also known as narrow money, M1 is the most liquid form of money and is made up of currency in circulation and demand deposits in banks.
 
 
 
• **M2**
 
 
• A broader concept of money supply, M2 includes M1 plus savings deposits with post office savings banks.
 
 
 
• **M3**
 
 
• Also known as broad money or aggregate monetary resource, M3 includes M1 plus time deposits with the bank.
 
 
 
• **M4**
 
 
• Includes all items of M3 plus total deposits of post office saving accounts.
 
 
 
• These measures are in decreasing order of liquidity, with M1 being the most liquid and M4 being the least liquid. 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India publishes figures for these four alternative measures of money supply
